problem: Given that $m\ge 1$ is an integer, simplify $\frac{(2m)!\,(m+4)!}{(m+5)!\,(2m-1)!}.$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}(m+1)! & =(m+1)\cdot m! \\ m! & =m\cdot (m-1)!\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we can cancel the $m!$ and $(m-1)!$ that occur in both the numerator and the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(m!)^{2}}{(m+1)!\,(m-1)!} & =\frac{m!\cdot m!}{(m+1)!\,(m-1)!} \\  & =\frac{m!\cdot m\cdot (m-1)!}{(m+1)\cdot m!\cdot (m-1)!} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{m!}\cdot m\cdot \cancel{(m-1)!}}{(m+1)\cdot \cancel{m!}\cdot \cancel{(m-1)!}} \\  & =\frac{m}{m+1}\end{aligned}
$$
